question: An 11-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with a 12-hour history of severe abdominal pain. She says that the pain started near the middle of her abdomen and moved to the right lower quadrant after about 10 hours. Several hours after the pain started she also started experiencing nausea and loss of appetite. On presentation, her temperature is 102.5°F (39.2°C), blood pressure is 115/74 mmHg, pulse is 102/min, and respirations are 21/min. Physical exam reveals rebound tenderness in the right lower quadrant. Raising the patient's right leg with the knee flexed significantly increases the pain. Which of the following is the most common cause of this patient's symptoms in children?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Severe abdominal pain" -> "Pain localized to right lower quadrant" -> "Rebound tenderness present" -> "Increased pain with right leg raise" -> "Signs suggestive of appendicitis" -> "Most common cause in children is fecalith obstruction" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Severe abdominal pain" -> "Nausea and loss of appetite" -> "Fever present" -> "Physical exam shows rebound tenderness" -> "Symptoms consistent with appendicitis" -> "Fecalith obstruction is a common cause in children" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Abdominal pain starts in the middle" -> "Pain migrates to right lower quadrant" -> "Fever and tachycardia present" -> "Rebound tenderness indicates possible inflammation" -> "Most likely diagnosis is appendicitis" -> "Fecalith obstruction is the most common cause in children" -> 88%

CHAIN: "Right lower quadrant pain" -> "Associated nausea and fever" -> "Physical exam reveals rebound tenderness" -> "Pain with leg raise suggests irritation" -> "Appendicitis is likely" -> "Fecalith obstruction is a frequent cause in pediatric cases" -> 87%

CHAIN: "Severe abdominal pain" -> "Pain migrates to right lower quadrant" -> "Fever and tachycardia noted" -> "Rebound tenderness indicates inflammation" -> "Appendicitis is suspected" -> "Lymphoid hyperplasia can cause appendicitis but less common than fecalith" -> 75%
analysis: The clinical presentation of severe abdominal pain that migrates to the right lower quadrant, accompanied by fever, nausea, and rebound tenderness, is highly suggestive of appendicitis. In children, the most common cause of appendicitis is fecalith obstruction, which can lead to inflammation and infection of the appendix. Other options like lymphoid hyperplasia and Meckel diverticulum are less common causes of acute abdominal pain in this age group. Therefore, fecalith obstruction is the most likely cause in this scenario.
